rationale: Foliate (GPL-3.0, COPYING) is an open file-based desktop e-book reader built with GJS/GTK4 that matches the leaf's defining core: one opened book, a paginated or scrolled reading surface (src/reader/reader.js sets flow to 'paginated' or 'scrolled'), in-book movement (prev/next/goLeft/goRight/scrollUp/scrollDown), and a per-book position persisted outside the session: src/data.js keys each book to its own JSON file through src/utils.js JSONStorage, while src/book-viewer.js writes 'progress' and 'lastLocation' (an EPUB CFI, i.e. a text anchor) on every relocation and restores it when the book is opened again. Small source surface, no store, no accounts.

scenario.name: Resume a book exactly where reading stopped
scenario.audience: A person reading one long-form EPUB over several sittings on a Linux desktop
scenario.objective: Reopen the same book days later and land on the exact passage where reading stopped, even after the typography changed
workflow: Open one EPUB from the file chooser; it renders as a paginated reading surface with a progress slider and table of contents
Turn pages or scroll to read; each relocation updates that book's own JSON file with progress and the CFI of the current position
Close the application, then reopen the same file
Change font size or margins; the book re-paginates but the saved position still points at the same text
acceptance: Reopening the same EPUB restores the same passage (CFI), not merely a similar percentage
Each book keeps its own position: a second book opens at its own last position, unaffected by the first
The stored position is a text anchor, so it survives a font-size change that alters the page count
Page turns and the progress slider visibly change the position value stored in that book's JSON file
